title: KV cache invalidation race caused model-version mismatch and rollforward failure
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: During a staged rollout of v3 of the conversational model to a subset of traffic, a race in the KV cache invalidation path allowed requests to be served with a mixture of v2 kernel state and v3 model parameters. The hybrid state caused a class of inference errors and tokenization mismatch leading to elevated errors and a failed automated rollforward. The incident required manual intervention to rehydrate caches and pause the rollout. This document captures timeline, root cause analysis, impact, temporary mitigations, and long-term action items.
impact_summary: Incident lasted ~47 minutes with 12% error rate spike for affected region (us-west-2) and increased tail latency up to 3x for ~6% of requests. No customer data was leaked. Several mid-market customers reported degraded response quality; one integration saw a transient 5xx spike and temporarily throttled traffic.
timeline: 2025-02-18T10:03:12Z - Canary rollout of model v3 initiated (10% traffic in us-west-2).
2025-02-18T10:09:40Z - Error monitoring alert: inference error rate increased from baseline 0.2% to 8.7% for canary route.
2025-02-18T10:12:05Z - Oncall alerted, started live debugging. Initial hypothesis: tokenization mismatch between model variants.
2025-02-18T10:19:30Z - Observed mismatch in model signature and KV cache keys; some requests used v2 KV entries but v3 parameters.
2025-02-18T10:25:14Z - Automated rollback attempted by rollout controller but rollback failed due to partial pin state and queued requests relying on stale cache entries.

2025-02-18T10:33:02Z - Mitigation: paused canary, drained in-flight requests, and issued a coordinated cache invalidation + rewarm procedure. Manual rollforward to fully v3 was aborted; decision made to keep v2 until fixes deployed.
2025-02-18T10:50:00Z - Traffic normalized; monitoring showed error rate and latency returning to baseline by 10:55.
2025-02-18T11:00:00Z - Incident declared mitigated; post-incident triage scheduled.
root_cause: A race between deployment lifecycle hooks and the KV cache invalidation path allowed requests to be dispatched to workers where the model binary had been swapped but the worker's KV cache had not been atomically invalidated. The rollout controller assumed cache eviction would be synchronous; however, the cache invalidation RPC is eventually consistent across shard boundaries. Under load, some workers served requests using stale KV entries referencing v2 keyspace while new kernel code expected v3 kv shapes, producing errors and corrupted token outputs. The rollback controller did not account for in-flight requests referencing mismatched cache state, causing rollback to hang until manual draining occurred.
mitigation: Immediate actions taken during incident: paused canary rollout; triggered cluster-wide cache invalidation RPC; drained workers then warmed caches with v3 traffic in a controlled manner; added temporary gating to rollout controller to ensure cache invalidation ack before routing traffic. Rolling fix prevented further mixed-serve occurrences for remainder of day.
action_items: ENG-99124 - Make KV cache invalidation synchronous in rollout path or add explicit quorum ack (owner: Omar Patel, due: 2025-03-09).
ENG-99125 - Update rollout controller to block automated rollback/promotion until in-flight request drain and cache stabilization complete (owner: Leila Gomez, due: 2025-03-16).
ENG-99126 - Add end-to-end integration test that simulates shard-level eventual consistency and validates no mixed-serve under concurrent model swap (owner: Priya Singh, due: 2025-04-01).
ENG-99127 - Instrument per-worker KV cache version headers in traces and logs for faster detection (owner: Omar Patel, due: 2025-03-02).
ENG-99128 - Create an ops runbook for coordinated cache invalidation + drain + rewarm during rollouts (owner: Oncall Team, due: 2025-03-05).
ENG-99129 - Post-deployment, run targeted canaries with synthetic prompts measuring tokenization/response divergence for 30 minutes before wider rollout (owner: SRE, due: 2025-03-12).
